Tasks: 280 chains of 20 requests (140 Python repositories), hidden developer tests. Configurations: ten models in one harness (mini-swe-agent 2.4.6); controlled settings AGENT CODE vs HUMAN CODE (authorship), SILENT CONTINUATION (verification), VERIFIED (external feedback), REVIEW (cross-model review, 2,180 items per reviewer), harness comparison on 58 chains. Baseline: human-code foundation and autonomous run as paired controls. Held constant: harness, specifications, budgets, grader, offline sealed images; reasoning settings differ per model and do not equalize compute. Acceptance tests: hidden F2P/P2P tests of requests 1..k after every request. Repetitions: eight independent attempts per chain in AUTONOMOUS; one attempt per arm in VERIFIED and harness comparisons. Human intervention: none

Claude Opus 5.5 best (pass@1 66.7%), separated from every other model (p <= 0.036); four tiers: Opus 5.5, Opus 5, seven models 45-52%, Opus 4.8. Average chain completion 51% vs 66-84% request completion; strict pass@1 averages 39%. Verified agent code is nearly as good a foundation as human code (gap -3.6 to +0.8 pp); one unverified mistake raises next-request failure by about 18 pp on average. No reviewer discriminates wrong from correct code (Youden J <= 0.15). One 'verification failed' message lifts average pass@1 from 51% to 59% (+1 to +22 pp, 7 of 10 intervals above zero) but raises regressions 3-9 pp; naming failing tests repairs more misses than repeating the bare message

Distinguished configurations partly (leader and bottom model separated; seven mid models mostly not separable). Repeatable: eight attempts per chain with bootstrap intervals and paired tests; pass@8 vs pass@1 shows same chains fail all models. Limitations stated: fixed-test correctness only, not user intent or readability; Python-only, small repositories; twenty requests need not form a twenty-link dependency chain; pass@1 judges only the final state; specifications model-written and model-audited, not human-reviewed; possible memorization (three Claude models reproduce 14-19% of sampled change blocks) not excluded

Limitations as above (Section 6). Gaps / recommendations: model builders should make certifying a request as much a goal as implementing it (agents cannot tell wrong from correct work, repair only part of misses); system builders should keep a verification channel to the agent and widen what the verifier sees; benchmark builders should grade agents in chains, report completion with and without a supervisor and publish hidden contracts; users should check each request before building on it

Post hoc 14-chain exclusion documented in App. D.10 (p. 11, 30). Amazon Bedrock served most evaluated models (p. 33).
